text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Urology consultation to share survivorship surveillance after radical cystectomy, review the stoma, and set the metabolic monitoring plan
  • Cancer surveillance after cystectomy for pT2a N0 disease: CT or MRI of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis every 6 to 12 months for 2 to 3 years, then yearly; no adjuvant therapy
  • Kidney and metabolic monitoring after an ileal conduit: chemistry with creatinine, chloride, and bicarbonate every 3 to 6 months in the first year, then yearly; upper-tract imaging every 6 months to year 3; vitamin B12 yearly; alkali for bicarbonate below 22 mmol/L
  • Stoma care with the wound, ostomy, and continence nurse: appliance fitting, peristomal skin care, and parastomal hernia checks
  • Urine infection plan with a conduit: no routine urine cultures or treatment of bacteriuria without symptoms; for fever, flank pain, or rigors, a culture taken by catheter from the stoma and prompt treatment; about 2 liters of fluid a day
  • Distress screening at each visit, physical activity, and a written survivorship care plan

resource.title: Hubert H. Humphrey synthetic care plan
resource.description: Primary care after radical cystoprostatectomy with an ileal conduit for urothelial bladder cancer, on the AUA/ASCO/SUO muscle-invasive bladder cancer guideline, the AUA/SUO non-muscle-invasive guideline, and the CMID urologic cancer monograph: how high-risk non-muscle-invasive disease that recurs after intravesical therapy and earlier pelvic radiation leads to early cystectomy, and how often the final pathology is upstaged; why pT2a N0 disease needs no adjuvant therapy; surveillance by cross-sectional imaging every 6 to 12 months and upper-tract and kidney function checks every 6 months; the metabolic effects of an ileal conduit (hyperchloremic acidosis, kidney function, vitamin B12); stoma and peristomal skin care; and the difference between expected bacteriuria in conduit urine and a true kidney infection, with a culture taken by catheter from the stoma. His documented history of bladder growths, intravesical thiotepa with X-ray therapy, and a radical cystectomy with a small-intestine conduit frames the episode.
